subtype: Glee when the sibling is scolded [Actor]
passage: It was a rushed morning: the power had gone, the water was cold, and the school van was due in ten minutes. Gurleen, eight, knocked over the milk, and Mummy snapped, "Gurleen! Look what you've done! Now we're late!" Five-year-old Kishore was pulling on his socks. Only yesterday Gurleen had told Mummy he'd drawn on the wall. A smile crept onto his face. He hid it behind his knee. Then Gurleen's eyes filled as she mopped, and Kishore looked down at his socks for a long time. When the van honked, he pushed his biscuit into her hand.

qa.q: What had Gurleen told Mummy the day before?
qa.a: That Kishore had drawn on the wall.

qa.q: Why did a smile creep onto Kishore's face when Gurleen was scolded?
qa.a: She had told on him the day before, so seeing her in trouble felt like the score was even.

qa.q: What did Kishore choose to do after his smile faded, and why did it matter?
qa.a: He pushed his biscuit into Gurleen's hand, a small way to make up for the smirk and comfort her.

qa.q: What was the morning like for Gurleen?
qa.a: Rushed and upsetting: she was scolded, her eyes filled as she mopped, and then Kishore quietly gave her his biscuit.

grounding: A young boy smirks when Gurleen is scolded, because she told on him, then looks away and makes a small amends.

subtype: Glee when the sibling is scolded [Actor]
passage: In their Chennai flat, Appa held up the cracked remote. "Seema, how many times have I said, no throwing things?" Seven-year-old Seema stared at the floor. Four-year-old Leela, on the sofa, felt a funny bubble in her tummy. Her big sister always got the stars and the "good girl". Leela's mouth twitched into a small smirk. Seema glanced up and saw it. Leela's smile vanished. She turned her face into the cushion and stayed very still while Appa finished. Later she left the sparkly hairclip that Seema loved on Seema's pillow.

qa.q: What did Appa hold up?
qa.a: The cracked remote.

qa.q: What made Leela feel "a funny bubble" when Seema was scolded?
qa.a: Seema usually got the stars and the "good girl", so seeing her in trouble made Leela feel her own place was a little safer.

qa.q: What did Leela do after hiding in the cushion, and was it a good choice?
qa.a: She left the sparkly hairclip Seema loved on Seema's pillow, a quiet way to say sorry for the smirk.

qa.q: How might Seema have felt seeing Leela's smirk?
qa.a: Already in trouble, Seema probably felt hurt and alone, as if her little sister was enjoying it 😔

grounding: A small girl smirks when her praised older sister is scolded, then hides her face and quietly makes amends.

subtype: Glee when the sibling is scolded [Actor]
passage: "Uday, it's dark! I said home by six!" Mumma's voice filled the doorway. "Sorry, Mumma, the match went on..." Behind the sofa, six-year-old Pallavi giggled. "Pallavi, is this funny?" The giggle stopped. "No." "Then why are you smiling?" Pallavi picked at a sofa thread. "He always gets to go out late. I never do." Mumma sat down. "So you were glad he's in trouble?" Pallavi nodded, shook her head, nodded again. "A little. Now I feel bad." Uday sniffed. "Thanks a lot." "Sorry, bhaiya." Mumma pulled them both close. "Tomorrow, Pallavi comes to the match too. Till six."

qa.q: By what time was Uday supposed to be home?
qa.a: By six.

qa.q: How did Pallavi feel about Uday being scolded, and what shows it?
qa.a: Mixed: a little glad, because he always gets to go out late, and then bad about it. She nodded, shook her head and nodded again.

qa.q: What did Mumma do that helped Pallavi, and why did it work?
qa.a: Mumma calmly asked why Pallavi was smiling and then let Pallavi go to the match too, dealing with the unfairness behind the glee.

qa.q: How did Uday feel hearing Pallavi's giggle?
qa.a: Hurt and a bit annoyed ("Thanks a lot"), since his little sister seemed to be enjoying his trouble.

grounding: A young girl giggles when her brother is told off, since he gets freedoms she lacks, and then feels bad.

subtype: Glee when the sibling is scolded [Actor]
passage:
Note from Rosy, after-school carer, Monday.
Tarun (8) kicked the football into the flowerpots again, and his mother scolded him at the gate. His brother Nilesh (5), beside me, pressed his lips together to hide a grin. That morning Tarun had grabbed the last banana and teased him. Then Nilesh looked at Tarun's red face and quickly away, and fiddled with his shoelace.
At snack time, unasked, he pushed half his biscuit across to Tarun.
Later I told Nilesh, "It's okay to feel a bit glad, and a bit bad after." He leaned on my arm. I'll tell their mother how kind he was.

qa.q: What did Nilesh push across to Tarun at snack time?
qa.a: Half of his biscuit.

qa.q: Why might Nilesh have looked away and fiddled with his shoelace?
qa.a: He seemed to feel guilty after his grin, seeing Tarun's red face while he himself was safe.

qa.q: What did Rosy do with Nilesh later, and why could it help?
qa.a: Rosy told him it's okay to feel a bit glad and a bit bad after, which lets him understand his feelings without shame.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel receiving half a biscuit from his brother?
qa.a: Tarun might feel surprised and comforted, especially after being scolded at the gate.

grounding: A carer notes a young child grinning at his brother's scolding, then looking away guilty and making amends.

subtype: Glee when the sibling is scolded [Actor]
passage: In Aaji's yard in Palus, the goat had got into the brinjal patch again. "Ganga! Who left the gate open?" Aaji shouted, hands on hips. Ganga, nine, hung her head. Tushar, five, sat on the step with his slate. Only yesterday Ganga had got the biggest mango and a pat on the head from Aaji. A small smile crept across Tushar's face. Then Ganga looked up and saw it. Tushar's smile vanished. He stared hard at his slate and scribbled nothing. Later, when Ganga sat alone by the well, he came over, held out a guava from his pocket and waited.

qa.q: What did the goat get into?
qa.a: The brinjal patch in Aaji's yard.

qa.q: Why did Tushar's smile vanish when Ganga looked up?
qa.a: He seemed to feel guilty the moment his sister saw him enjoying her trouble.

qa.q: What small step did Tushar take to make up, and why did it help?
qa.a: He brought Ganga a guava and waited beside her, showing he was sorry without needing words.

qa.q: How might Ganga feel seeing her brother smile while she was scolded?
qa.a: She might feel hurt or annoyed, and then softened when he came to the well with the guava.

grounding: A young child smiles at his sister's scolding after she was favoured, then looks away guilty and makes amends.
